idea-plugin.name: TraceWeave - Code Flow Tracker
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.1

  • Connect the Flow: Choose a Way opens with the first way found and the others join the list while the search goes on. Pause / Resume (it goes on from where it paused), Load More (10 ways at a time, off when there are no others) and a colored state: searching, completed, paused or failed. Cancel stops the search at once.
  • Flow Diagram Sync (before Settings): saves by itself, the layout (positions, lines, looks, notes; the default) or everything; the History marks the saved steps. Ctrl+click Close (or a tab's ✕) closes all the tabs, asking once per tab with changes.
  • Debug Data: one toolbar for the value (a view button with ▾, Expand / Collapse following the selection, Find showing the field filter, Settings with the fields' order and Hide Internals); hidden while nothing is selected. Add, Edit, Remove and Reset work on a line's values too (+ adds a new value at the line). Editing a value saved with internals edits it as shown ("BK-1042", not its bytes).
  • The Flow window's line numbers have room for 6 digits: a tag's bar no longer covers them. Menus open right under their button, with a small gap.

1.4.0

  • New: Stop at Value tab. Stop the debugger on the line where a value shows up (e.g. BK-1044), without breakpoints of your own: anywhere in the project's code (fast field watches), at the flow's lines, wherever the debugger stops, or stepping from where it is paused. Several values (each on or off, any or all of them), several records running at once, Waiting for Debug until the app runs in Debug.
  • New: Watch a Field or Object: a field (BookingDto.status), every field of a class, a method's local variable or parameter (BookingWorkflow.book().booking), a field inside it (.email, .getEmail(), .setEmail()) or what a method returns (.return). Stop when it is set, changes, becomes null or holds a value; optionally when the object's data changes. Class.method() lists the method's variables to pick. Also from the editor: right-click → TraceWeave → Watch….
  • Stop at Value: every stop listed (when, where, thread, what was found) with filters and order; the variables at a stop as a tree (like Threads & Variables) or JSON, with bookmarks; To Debug Data copies stops into the active flow; a Recycle Bin for records and stops; Start in green, Stop in red.
  • Hide Internals (Debug Data, Compare, Compare Pasted Data, Stop at Value; on by default): a String saved as its bytes shows as its text, and what Java, Kotlin, Scala, Groovy, .NET, Python and JavaScript keep inside values (compiler fields, $id / $type, __dunder__ names…) is left out.
  • Debug Data: bookmarks (a field to the top of its object, shared with Stop at Value); a line's values shown together; buttons that shrink to icons and wrap.
  • Flow Diagram, Connect the Flow: the ways panel previews a way on hover, can be minimized, dragged and opened full screen (Choose a Way previews on hover too and keeps the clicked way); ways already on the tab are left out.
  • Flow Diagram lines: drag a line by its handles (the selected line is the one grabbed), around a box or into its side; drag a note along its line; Reset Line Route. Lines keep apart where there is room, notes have their own lane. Auto Layout lines boxes up with the rows that call them and resets dragged lines.
  • Flow Diagram: Find (Ctrl+F), Add File suggestions (open, recent and project files), the open diagram follows lines added to the flow, a restyled Connect to popup, mouse-wheel scrolling everywhere.

1.3.2

  • Flow Diagram tabs: one tab per flow, like a browser's. + opens a new or saved flow; right-click a tab to rename its flow, color it, connect it with another tab, close it or delete its flow. Empty flows are deleted when the window closes.
  • Flow Diagram: select several classes (Ctrl+click, Ctrl+A), copy, cut and paste them, or move / copy them to another tab (or a new one). Moved classes leave orange link boxes (⇄ in “the other tab”) on both sides, and a tab with both combined opens, connected where the code makes the calls.
  • Connect the Flow: right-click a method in the Flow Diagram → Connect the Flow to…, or select two lines in the Flow tab → Connect the Flow Between These Lines. The calls between them are read from the code and added (e.g. main() → bookTrip(), both lines that call getDestination() → getDestination()).
  • Flow Diagram buttons: Close · Save · Reset, with Close All, Don't Save and Close All, Save and Close All, and Save All in their ▾ menus. Auto Layout puts every call left to right. Dashed lines only for calls connected by hand; a selected call glows.
  • Flow Diagram code panel: + adds a line, − takes one out (not a line whose call is drawn to another box); double-click opens the line in the editor, Ctrl+click goes to a name's code. Fixed: the code panel stayed green and empty in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2.
  • Debug Data: a Flow button with the flows (as in the Flow tab), a Settings button, names for lines, delete flows, and the Flow tab's look. Flows are shared with the Flow tab (new, selected, deleted), names are not. Its shortcuts (Delete, Ctrl+C, F2, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+F...) work again.
  • Compare: Open File… and Export… (Old, New, the differences); OLD and NEW are clearly marked. Comparing pasted data or files shows the result in the same window.
  • Delete Flows… deletes several flows at once. Exported files start with the project's name. The Markdown diagrams name each file's project.
  • New Flow Diagram and Grouped View icons.

1.3.1

  • The plugin ID is io.github.rameshnr.flowtracker again (1.3.0 had a new one), so TraceWeave updates Flow Tracker like any update. If you installed 1.3.0 from GitHub, uninstall it first (Settings → Plugins): your flows, settings and saved debug values are kept.

1.3.0

  • New name: TraceWeave - Code Flow Tracker (was Flow Tracker). Your flows, settings, saved debug values and shortcuts are kept.
  • Works in IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1 and every later version (1.2.1 needed 2026.2 or later). Checked with the Plugin Verifier against 2023.1, 2023.3, 2024.2, 2025.1, 2025.2, 2026.2 and 2026.3.
  • Debug Data: right-click a variable in the debugger's Variables view → Save to TraceWeave. Compare it with the same variable saved at that line in another flow or debug run (or with its value now), find names, keys and values in all saved values and in the current debug session, edit saved values with a history to revert, and restore deleted ones from the Recycle Bin.
  • Flow Diagram: Add File / Class asks for a file, then one of its classes; a file that isn't in the project becomes a custom class named after it (its file can be changed later). Add Method offers a custom method for a new name. The Custom Class and Custom Method buttons are gone.
  • Flow Diagram: boxes show their project; notes on calls (at the middle of the arrow, and in the sequence diagram); tag a method Bug, Important or Question.
  • Tags show at the start of a line in the panel (a coloured bar and the tag before the code).
  • Copy ▾ → Copy Original Log copies only the Original Log as plain text.
  • New Flow Diagram and Clear icons.
  • More languages: C#, C / C++, Go, Rust, Swift, PHP, Dart, Scala (by their { } blocks), Python and Ruby (by indentation), and libraries' decompiled .class files (also found by Add File). The Flow Diagram's buttons say Add File and Add Function.
  • Debug Data: save values from the editor (a selected expression or the variable at the caret), from Evaluate Expression results, or with Add Expression; show a value as JSON or text, copy it and export it. Compare matches map entries by key and ignores instance ids (HotelService@1141), so only real changes show.
  • Flow Diagram: notes on calls take the first free spot on their arrow, so they don't cover each other or boxes; the window opens at once and only once, however often its button is clicked. It is a normal window (it doesn't block the IDE) with the system's Minimize, Maximize and Close. Notes on calls get a shape and background, text and border colors; custom classes get a project.
  • Debug Data: a clearer Compare (changed / added / removed counts, map entries as key = value), Compare as JSON in IntelliJ's diff viewer, and Compare Pasted Data (JSON, XML, toString() or text, detected and laid out line by line). Fixed: values read while the debugger was still collecting them could be incomplete.
  • Debug Data: Export the selected (or all) saved values with their edit history to a .flowdebug.json file, and Import such a file.
  • Debug Data: Capture Data saves each variable by itself while debugging, where the debugger stops or at every line it runs up to the next breakpoint, all of them or only the line's; Compare opens the saved value next to an empty side to paste the other one (Ctrl+Enter compares); Layout: side by side or top and bottom (Auto when narrow); keys Delete, Ctrl+D, F2, Ctrl+F; New Value, Add / Edit / Remove Field and Copy (value, name = value, JSON) that know maps, lists and objects (an object can be added as JSON); edit a value as JSON or text and Apply, or Reset it to the saved data; every change revertible in History; Add Field lists the class's own and inherited fields; added values get types like the debugger's; Compare marks Old and New and can swap them, and edits both sides (Tree, JSON, Text) with Undo, Redo, History (with the saved values' own changes), Reset and "See what changed"; Add Field doesn't add a field or key twice; copy, remove and delete several at once, Copy Children as JSON and Paste; the value tree stays open while you edit; Add Expression is enabled only while the debugger is paused; the value's Tree / JSON / Text / Copy / Save As buttons wrap; clearer Delete and Recycle Bin icons.
  • Flow Diagram and Compare windows get the color of IntelliJ's main header; a class's project is shown in a band on top of its box; "text only" notes are no longer crossed by their arrow; several calls from (or to) one method start (or end) at their own spots, and the one going further away takes its own way, so they don't look like one call that branches; call notes keep off other calls' lines.
  • Flow Diagram: Apply asks to confirm the changes (and no longer asks to discard them); Cancel asks once; the project band can have its own background, border and text format, and shows in the sequence diagram too.
  • Fixed: connecting a call by hand in the Flow Diagram sent the calling line to the Recycle Bin on Apply; the Copy menu showed its title twice.

1.2.1

  • Flow Diagram: the flow as an editable diagram. Add classes and files (JSP, JavaScript, TLD...) and methods from the project (search as you type, a pattern such as *Cruise*.java or a /regex/) and pick the method lines to add, or add custom ones (drawn in amber) that aren't in the code yet; rename and remove them, and draw calls between methods. Apply writes the changes to the flow as one undoable step; Cancel keeps it as it was. A History with Undo / Redo stays after Apply, and changes that change nothing aren't added to it.
  • Flow Diagram: Change Class and Rename Class list the matching classes as you type; a name no class has becomes a custom class. The buttons say Add File / Class, Add Method / Function, Custom Class / File and Custom Method / Function.
  • Flow Diagram: Format a box (themes Plain, Light, Dark and eight colors, or its own class section, method section and border colors with text that stays readable), class, file and method names and notes (bold, italic, underline, strike-through, color), and a call's line (dashes, dots, double lines, widths, curved / straight / elbow, arrow ends, color), with notes under class and method names. Reset in each Format window, and Reset Theme for the whole diagram. Saved with the flow on Apply and in Export / Import.
  • Flow Diagram: boxes never overlap (the others make room when a box grows or is dropped on another) and lines go around boxes in their way. Zoom buttons in the bottom right corner, Ctrl+mouse wheel and Ctrl+Plus / Minus / 0; drag an empty spot to move the view.
  • Flow Diagram: click a method to see its lines of code under the diagram, with syntax colors; View Full Code shows the whole file at that method.
  • Flow Diagram: Copy PNG and Copy Sequence PNG copy the diagram, or its calls as a sequence diagram, as an image, with a light or dark background (split buttons). Settings for the images' default background and the window's background, and a Dark / Light switch in the drawing area.
  • Settings: Use IntelliJ Theme takes every Flow Tracker color from the current IntelliJ theme and editor color scheme (off: Flow Tracker's own colors).
  • Fixed: Copy, Open Markdown and Flow Diagram failing with an UnsupportedOperationException (Sync), and Export Flow refreshing the new file on the UI thread.
  • No deprecated or internal IntelliJ Platform API in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.2 and 2026.3 (Plugin Verifier): ReadAction.computeBlocking, JBUIScale.scale, OpenFileDescriptor.navigate for Walk-through and Open Markdown, and the version in Info is read from the plugin itself.

1.2.0

  • Nest Calls in Original Log: each called method's lines sit under the line that calls it, in Grouped and Flat View (on by default; a Settings switch). The project is named only when it changes.
  • Connect Call To: join a line by hand to the method it reaches (e.g. an API call into another project); used by Sync, the diagrams and the Original Log, and saved with the flow.
  • Sync Files, Copy as Markdown, Sequence Diagram and Copy All Flows are on by default.
  • The Flows popup lines up with the flow button, with a small gap below the buttons for all popups.
  • Vendor: RameshNR.

1.1.1

  • New plugin ID for JetBrains Marketplace (io.github.rameshnr.flowtracker). If you installed 1.1.0 from a zip, uninstall it first: your saved flows are kept.
  • Plugin icon, and screenshots in the plugin description.
  • MIT license.

1.1.0

  • Add to Flow Tracker from the editor (right-click or Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A), step numbers in the gutter, and lines that follow edits in both views.
  • Open Markdown: the flow as a .md file with the preview. Calls between JavaScript functions get arrows.
  • Screenshot carousel in the Info dialog.
  • Support for JSP / tag files, JavaScript / TypeScript (JS, JSX, TS, TSX), TLD, XML, HTML, Groovy, properties, YAML and SQL files.
  • Recycle Bin for deleted lines and flows; Copy All Flows.
  • Diagrams follow the real calls whatever order the lines are listed in (including JSP pages calling Java methods), are titled by file name, and give unconnected code (e.g. Java and JavaScript) separate diagrams.
  • Markdown lines are a table (line, syntax-highlighted code, note) instead of numbers mixed into the code, and each flow ends with its Original Log (the plain Grouped / Flat copy).
  • The Delete key removes selected items from the Recycle Bin.
  • Drag flows to reorder them.
  • Named flows per project, with Export / Import as .flow.json to share with your team.
  • Record a flow while debugging.
  • Walk-through: Next / Previous Step (Alt+] / Alt+[).
  • Mermaid sequence diagram option for the Markdown copy.
  • Search box, colour tags, warnings for lines that no longer match the code, and Kotlin support.
  • Row action bar order is now Copy, Note | Delete.

1.0.0

  • Grouped and Flat views with syntax-colored code blocks and project tags.
  • Hover action bar (move, copy, note, delete), drag and drop, right-click menu.
  • Sync: automatic call order across files.
  • Copy formats: default text, optimized flat log, Markdown with a Mermaid flow diagram.
  • Undo / Redo for adding and removing lines.
  • Settings popup and Info dialog.
